query_snapshot: For hydrogen chloride, which barriers does the archived NIOSH table place in its 8-hour and 4-hour groups, and what additional hazard language appears in the entry?
final_answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- The archived NIOSH table places the following materials in the 8-hour (8 hr) barrier group for hydrogen chloride: Butyl; Teflon; Saranex; Barricade; Responder; Trellchem; Tychem. [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective ...: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- The archived NIOSH table places the following materials in the 4-hour (4 hr) barrier group for hydrogen chloride: Neoprene; PVC. [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective ...: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- The archived NIOSH table includes the hazard language for hydrogen chloride: “Prevent skin contact (solution) / Frostbite” and the note “Prevent possible skin freezing from direct liquid contact.” [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective ...: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
